ddl:
CREATE TABLE Customer (
    Address VARCHAR(255),
    Contact_person VARCHAR(255),
    Credit_rating VARCHAR(255),
    Customer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Customer_name VARCHAR(255),
    Customer_type VARCHAR(255),
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Phone INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE Product (
    Brand VARCHAR(255),
    Inventory_quantity INTEGER,
    Product_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Product_category VARCHAR(255),
    Product_name VARCHAR(255),
    Production_date DATETIME,
    Specifications VARCHAR(255),
    Supplier VARCHAR(255),
    Unit_price FLOAT
);

CREATE TABLE Customer_product_purchase (
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Order_status VARCHAR(255),
    Order_time DATETIME,
    Payment_method VARCHAR(255),
    Payment_status VARCHAR(255),
    Payment_time DATETIME,
    Product_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Product_quantity INTEGER,
    Total_amount FLOAT,
    Unit_price FLOAT,
    PRIMARY KEY (Customer_ID, Product_ID, Order_time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Product_ID) REFERENCES Product(Product_ID)
);
gold_question: This is a customer management system. For customer management, the system maintains basic customer information (customer ID, customer name, contact person, etc.), records detailed customer information (address, phone, email, etc.), and manages customer classification information (customer type, credit rating). For product management, the system maintains basic product information (product ID, product name, specifications, etc.), records detailed product information (unit price, inventory quantity, production date, etc.), and manages product classification information (product category, brand, supplier, etc.). For purchase management, the system records order information (order time, order status, etc.), maintains order details (product quantity, unit price, total amount, etc.), and manages payment information (payment method, payment status, payment time, etc.).
